Do not go up… for I am not in the midst of you (Deuteronomy 1:42). Where have I rushed ahead without asking God?
Strive to excel in them for building up the church (1 Corinthians 14:12). How does my gift build up others?
Do not be afraid, little flock (Luke 12:32). What worry do I need to hand over to the Father tonight?
pm.resp: Father, we trust in you.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may not be afraid to go where the Spirit leads.
For leaders in government and in the Church, that they may defend the orphan and the widow and refuse every bribe.
For all who are anxious about money, health or the future, especially parents at the start of the school year.
For prayer groups and all who have spiritual gifts, that they may use them in love to build up the Church.
For farmers and for all affected by the monsoon rains, that they may be protected and blessed.
pm.close: Father, your Son told his little flock not to be afraid, because it is your pleasure to give us the kingdom. Deliver us from fear and from presumption, refine us in your love, and keep our hearts where our treasure is. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: you have many guardians in Christ but not many fathers; I became your father through the Gospel; be imitators of me.
The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.
Jesus: woe to anyone who puts a stumbling block before one of these little ones; cut off whatever causes you to sin.
St Justin, philosopher and martyr, left the oldest full description of the Sunday Eucharist.
2027-06-01.action: Pray once this week with a child, slowly and aloud, and remove one thing that leads you into sin.
2027-06-01.question: Is my faith more talk than power?

family.explain: Saint Paul says that he is like a father to the Christians in Corinth, because he told them about Jesus. He asks them to copy the way he lives. Jesus says that little children are very precious to God, and that nobody should ever lead a child to do wrong. Grown-ups must protect children, and children must tell a grown-up they trust if anyone makes them feel unsafe.
family.intention: We pray for children starting a new school year, and for their teachers.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we copy in our family, and is it a good example?”

illus: An illustration

On the first day of the new school year, a headmistress in a government school near Thrissur stood at the gate to greet the children. One small boy arrived crying, clutching his father's hand. The father was embarrassed and tried to push him in. The headmistress knelt down, took out a sweet, and asked the boy what he liked. ‘Drawing,’ he whispered. ‘Then you will draw the first picture on our new classroom wall,’ she said. Twenty years later, when that boy became a teacher himself, he said at his first staff meeting: ‘I do not remember a single lesson from that year. I remember a teacher who knelt down at the gate.’ Children learn first from the way they are treated.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you love the little ones and you want your kingdom to be seen in power, not in empty words. Send your Holy Spirit upon us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Who has been a father or mother in faith to me?
The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power (1 Corinthians 4:20). Where is my faith only words?
If any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones (Matthew 18:6). How do I protect the children around me?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). When have I been afraid to say that I am a Christian?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom come in power.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that pastors and parents may be true fathers and mothers in faith.
For children beginning the new school year, for their teachers and for all who work in schools.
For children who have been harmed, that they may be heard, protected and healed.
For Christian thinkers, teachers and students, that like St Justin they may seek the truth and find it in Christ.
For Christians who suffer for their faith today.
pm.close: Father, you raised up St Justin to proclaim Christ, the wisdom and power of God. Give us faithful hearts, protect the little ones, and make our lives a witness to your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Many Samaritans believed because of the woman's testimony: he told me everything I have ever done.
They asked Jesus to stay, and many more believed because of his word: we have heard for ourselves; this is truly the Saviour of the world.
Paul: work out your salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who is at work in you.
Do all things without murmuring, and shine like stars in the world, holding fast to the word of life.
2027-06-02.action: Tell one person, simply, what the Lord has done for you, and spend one whole day without complaining.
2027-06-02.question: Do I believe only because of what others told me, or have I heard Jesus for myself?

family.explain: A woman met Jesus at a well. She was so happy that she ran to her town and told everyone, “Come and see!” The people came, and they asked Jesus to stay. After two days they said, “Now we believe, not only because you told us, but because we have heard him ourselves.” Our parents and teachers tell us about Jesus, but Jesus wants to be our own friend too. We meet him when we pray, when we read the Bible and when we go to the Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for people who have never heard of Jesus, and for missionaries who bring him to them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us spend a little time alone with Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Pala, studying for a master's degree in Germany, was asked by a classmate why he still went to Mass when so few of his friends did. He thought for a moment and said: ‘When I was small, I went because my grandmother took me. She used to pray the rosary in a loud voice on the verandah every evening, and I prayed because she did. When I came here, I stopped for almost a year. Then one night, alone and anxious before an exam, I went into an empty church and sat there for an hour. I cannot explain it, but I knew he was there. Now I do not go because my grandmother told me. I go because I have met him myself.’ On his next visit home he told his grandmother the story. She only laughed and said, ‘That is all I was praying for.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Saviour of the world, we gather around you as the Samaritans gathered at the well. Stay with us, speak to us, and let us hear you for ourselves. Amen.
share: Many Samaritans believed because of the woman’s testimony (John 4:39). Whose witness first brought me to Jesus?
They asked him to stay with them (John 4:40). Do I give Jesus time to stay with me?
It is God who is at work in you (Philippians 2:13). Where do I see God at work in me now?
Do all things without murmuring (Philippians 2:14). What do I grumble about most?
pm.resp: Lord, stay with us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that every believer may become a witness like the woman at the well.
For people who live far from the Church, that they may hear Christ for themselves.
For catechism teachers and parents who hand on the faith, that their words may lead children to a personal meeting with Jesus.
For families and communities torn by complaining and quarrels, that they may learn gratitude.
For missionaries, that the Saviour of the world may be known through them.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the Saviour of the world and you are at work in us by your Spirit. Make us witnesses of what we have seen and heard, keep us from murmuring, and let us shine like stars in this generation. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus: a sower went out to sow; some seed fell on the path, some on the rock, some among thorns, and some into good soil.
The seed is the word of God; the cares, riches and pleasures of life can choke it.
The good soil holds the word fast in an honest and good heart and bears fruit with patient endurance.
Paul: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth; you are God's field, God's building.
2027-06-03.action: Keep one sentence from the Gospel all week, and refuse to take part in any talk that divides your parish.
2027-06-03.question: Which of the four soils is my heart today?

family.explain: When the monsoon comes, farmers sow seeds. Some seeds fall on the hard path and birds eat them. Some fall on rocks and dry up. Some fall among thorns and get choked. Some fall on good soil and grow into a big harvest. Jesus says that the seed is God's word. When we listen to the Bible and keep it in our hearts, it grows in us and makes us good and kind.
family.intention: We pray for farmers and for good rains this monsoon, and for those who suffer from floods.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one word of Jesus that our family will try to remember this week?”

illus: An illustration

An old farmer in Wayanad, whose parents had come from Travancore in the years of the migration to Malabar, took his grandson to the field on the first morning of the monsoon. The boy watched him throw the seed and asked why he threw it so widely, even near the path where the birds were waiting. ‘Because I do not know which handful will grow,’ the old man said. ‘My father taught me: sow generously, keep the field clean, and leave the rest to God.’ Then he took off his towel, knelt at the edge of the field and made the sign of the cross over the wet earth. The grandson, who is now a priest, says that whenever he preaches he remembers that morning. ‘I throw the seed,’ he says. ‘I do not know which word will grow. God gives the growth.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, sower of the word, we open our hearts to you. Make them good soil, take away what hardens them, and let your word bear fruit in us. Amen.
share: The seed is the word of God (Luke 8:11). How do I receive the word on Sunday?
These have no root (Luke 8:13). When has my faith fallen away in a time of testing?
Choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life (Luke 8:14). What chokes the word in me?
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth (1 Corinthians 3:6). Do I trust God with the fruit of my work?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts good soil.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that the word may be preached everywhere and received with honest hearts.
For parishes and dioceses wounded by divisions, that they may remember they are God's field and God's building.
For farmers in this season of sowing, for good rains, and for those affected by floods and landslides.
For the Church in Uganda and in all Africa, that the seed sown by the martyrs may keep bearing fruit.
For those whose faith has dried up in times of trial, that they may find roots again.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the sower and his word is the seed of eternal life. Give us honest and good hearts, keep us united as your field, and make us bear fruit with patient endurance. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Genesis: Abram yields the first choice of land to Lot for the sake of peace; God promises him all the land he sees.
Isaiah: the suffering Servant was wounded for our transgressions; by his bruises we are healed.
Paul: if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him, you will be saved.
John: a soldier pierced the side of Jesus, and at once blood and water came out; they will look on the one whom they have pierced.
2027-06-04.action: Keep the First Friday with confession, Holy Qurbana and adoration, and renew the consecration of your family to the Sacred Heart this evening.
2027-06-04.question: Is my heart becoming more like the Heart of Jesus, gentle and humble?
catechism: The Sacred Heart, sign and symbol of Christ's love.
The Church born from the pierced side.
Prayer to the Heart of Jesus.
The heart as the place of encounter and covenant.
kidsaint: St Margaret Mary Alacoque

Margaret Mary was a French sister who lived more than three hundred years ago. While she prayed before the Blessed Sacrament, Jesus showed her his Heart, burning with love for everyone, and asked that people honour his Heart and receive him in Holy Communion on the First Fridays of the month. Some of the other sisters did not believe her and made fun of her, but a holy priest, St Claude de la Colombière, helped her. Today the whole Church loves the Sacred Heart. Lesson: Jesus loves you with a real heart, and he wants your love in return!
2027-06-04.special: Feast of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Syro-Malabar, Third Friday of the Apostles); First Friday. Latin Church: solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus; World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests.
term: First Friday

The first Friday of each month, kept in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Following the revelations to St Margaret Mary Alacoque, the faithful go to confession, receive Holy Communion in reparation and spend time in adoration on the First Fridays; many keep nine First Fridays in a row. In Kerala parishes the First Friday often includes adoration and a special Qurbana. Malayalam: ആദ്യവെള്ളി.

family.explain: When Jesus died on the cross, a soldier pierced his side with a spear, and blood and water came out. That wound shows us how much Jesus loves us: he gave everything, even his Heart. The picture of the Sacred Heart in our home reminds us that Jesus loves our family and wants to live with us. Jesus also says, “Learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.” We can make our hearts like his by being gentle with each other and by making peace when we quarrel.
family.intention: We pray for our priests on this day, and for families who are divided.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be gentle and humble like the Heart of Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Kanjirappally had not spoken for three years after their father's death, because of a quarrel over the family land. The younger one felt the elder had taken the better plot near the road. One First Friday evening the elder brother's wife lit the lamp before the old picture of the Sacred Heart that had hung in the family house since their grandparents' time, and the children began the rosary. The elder brother found himself looking at the picture for a long time. The next morning he walked to his brother's house with the land papers and said, ‘Take the plot near the road. I do not want to lose my brother for a few cents of land.’ The younger brother wept and refused, and in the end they divided it again together. At the next First Friday Qurbana, the parish priest noticed both families sitting in the same pew.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, meek and humble of heart, we gather before your pierced Heart. Pour out on us the blood and water of your mercy, and make our hearts like yours. Amen.
share: Let there be no strife between you and me, for we are kindred (Genesis 13:8). Where do I need to yield for the sake of peace?
By his bruises we are healed (Isaiah 53:5). What wound do I bring to the Heart of Jesus today?
One believes with the heart and so is justified (Romans 10:10). Do I confess Jesus as Lord with my lips as well as my heart?
They will look on the one whom they have pierced (John 19:37). What do I see when I look at the Crucified?
pm.resp: Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, born from the pierced side of Christ, that she may be a home of mercy for all.
For priests, on this World Day of Prayer for their sanctification, that their hearts may be shaped by the Heart of the Good Shepherd.
For families divided by quarrels over land and money, that they may choose peace as Abram did.
For those who suffer in body or mind, that they may find rest in the Heart of Jesus.
For those who have stopped believing, that they may look on the One who was pierced and believe.
pm.close: Father, you opened the Heart of your Son on the Cross, and from it flowed the sacraments of the Church. Draw us to that fountain, wash us in the water, feed us with the blood, and make our hearts gentle and humble like his. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Genesis: God renames Sarai as Sarah and promises that she will bear a son and give rise to nations.
Isaiah: the Lord himself will give a sign: the young woman shall bear a son and name him Immanuel, fulfilled in the Virgin Mary.
Paul: God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.
Luke: after three days Mary and Joseph find Jesus in the Temple; his mother treasured all these things in her heart.
2027-06-05.action: Pray an act of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, and one decade of the rosary each day for peace.
2027-06-05.question: Do I keep God's word in my heart even when I do not understand it?
catechism: Redeemed in a more exalted fashion.
kidsaint: Sts Francisco and Jacinta Marto

Francisco and Jacinta were a brother and sister from a poor family in Fatima, in Portugal. In 1917, while they looked after sheep with their cousin Lucia, the Mother of God appeared to them. She spoke of her Immaculate Heart and asked them to pray the rosary every day for peace and for sinners. Francisco loved to sit quietly before the tabernacle to comfort Jesus; Jacinta offered little sacrifices for sinners. Both died young, after an illness, and Pope Francis declared them saints in 2017. Lesson: even children can pray every day for peace in the world!
2027-06-05.special: Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Syro-Malabar, Third Saturday of the Apostles; an important Marian feast). Latin calendar: the Immaculate Heart of Mary and St Boniface, both optional this year. World Environment Day.
term: Immaculate Heart

The heart of the Virgin Mary, never touched by sin, honoured as the sign of her inner life of faith, love and prayer: the heart that kept and pondered the word of God (Luke 2:19, 51) and was pierced by sorrow at the Cross (Luke 2:35). The devotion was given liturgical form by St John Eudes, spread after the apparitions at Fatima (1917), and the feast was extended to the whole Church by Pius XII in 1944. Malayalam: വിമലഹൃദയം.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he went with Mary and Joseph to Jerusalem for a feast. On the way home they could not find him. They searched for three days and were very worried. At last they found him in the Temple, talking with the teachers. Mary told him how worried they had been. Then Jesus went home with them and obeyed them. Mary kept all these things in her heart. Mary's heart was full of love for God and for Jesus, and she loves us too. We can tell her everything that worries us.
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or have run away, for their parents, and for peace in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What worry can our family give to Mother Mary today?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kottayam waited up one monsoon night when her sixteen-year-old son did not come home after a quarrel. His phone was switched off. Her husband drove around the town while she knelt at the family altar with the rosary, and after midnight she simply said, ‘Amma, you also searched for your son for three days. Keep mine in your heart.’ Near dawn the boy came in, soaked and silent; he had spent the night at a friend's house. She wanted to shout at him. Instead she gave him a towel and a cup of tea, and they talked only the next evening. Years later, when he was married with his own children, he told her, ‘That night I expected a fight. You gave me tea. I have never forgotten it.’ She told him that she had learned it from the Mother of God, who kept in her heart what she did not understand.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God and our Mother, your Immaculate Heart kept the word of God and loved Jesus with a perfect love. Pray with us, as you prayed with the apostles, that the Holy Spirit may fill our hearts. Amen.
share: She shall give rise to nations (Genesis 17:16). How has God done in my life what seemed impossible?
The Lord himself will give you a sign (Isaiah 7:14). Is my heart closed by fear like Ahaz, or open like Mary?
He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Do I believe that God has chosen me?
His mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). What do I need to keep and ponder, without understanding it yet?
pm.resp: Immaculate Heart of Mary, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, gathered like the apostles around the Mother of Jesus, that she may be filled with the Holy Spirit.
For peace in the world, especially in nations at war, through the intercession of the Immaculate Heart.
For parents anxious about their children, and for children who are lost, that they may be found.
For families, that they may pray the rosary together and keep God's word in their hearts.
For the care of creation on this World Environment Day, that we may protect the earth God has given us.
pm.close: God our Father, you filled the heart of the Virgin Mary with your grace and made her the Mother of your Son and of the Church. By her prayers, make our hearts pure, open to your word and faithful in every trial, and gather the nations in peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A woman ill for twelve years touches the cloak of Jesus in faith and is healed.
Jesus turns in the crowd to meet her and calls her daughter: go in peace.
Paul: the God of all consolation consoles us so that we may console others.
2027-06-07.action: Contact one person this week who is going through a suffering the Lord once helped you through.
2027-06-07.question: Do I press around Jesus like the crowd, or do I reach out to him in faith?

family.explain: A woman had been sick for twelve long years. She had spent all her money on doctors, and nobody helped her. She thought, ‘If I only touch his clothes, I will be well.’ She touched Jesus' cloak, and she was healed. Jesus stopped and looked for her, because he wanted to meet her, not only to heal her. He called her ‘Daughter’. Jesus notices everyone, even people that others do not see.
family.intention: We pray for people who have been sick for a long time, for families who spend a lot of money on treatment, and for children starting the new school year.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our school, street or parish do people not notice? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in a parish near Thrissur was asked to start a small group for parents of children with long illnesses. She said she knew nothing about medicine. The parish priest replied that this was not what they needed. Twenty years earlier her own son had been in and out of hospital for three years with a kidney disease, and she had spent nights on hospital benches with her rosary. At the first meeting she did not give advice. She told them where to sit in the hospital canteen when the ward was too noisy to pray, which nurse would explain a report patiently, and how she had learned to say only ‘Jesus, I touch your cloak’ when she was too tired for longer prayers. A young father wrote to her later: ‘You were the first person who understood without my explaining.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you noticed the woman in the crowd and called her daughter. We reach out to you now in faith. Touch our hearts with your Holy Spirit, and make us channels of your consolation. Amen.
share: She had endured much under many physicians (Mark 5:26). What long burden have I carried, and have I brought it to Jesus?
If I but touch his clothes, I will be made well (Mark 5:28). How do I reach out to Jesus in my daily life?
Who touched my clothes? (Mark 5:30). Do I believe that Jesus notices me personally?
The God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3). Whom can I console with the comfort I have received?
pm.resp: Lord, touch us and heal us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may notice and console the forgotten.
For those who have been ill for many years, and for families burdened by the cost of treatment.
For doctors, nurses and hospital chaplains, that they may bring the touch of Christ.
For students and teachers beginning a new school year in the monsoon season.
For those who feel invisible and unloved, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
pm.close: Father of mercies and God of all consolation, your Son turned in the crowd to find the one who touched him in faith. Heal our wounds, console us in every affliction, and send us to console others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God calls Abram to go to a land he will be shown; St Mariam Thresia followed a new path of service in the same obedience.
Sirach: gold is tested in the fire; Paul: Christ lives in me.
Jesus: just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.
2027-06-08.action: Visit or help one family that is carrying a burden alone this week.
2027-06-08.question: Where is Christ waiting for me in the least of my neighbours?
kidsaint: St Mariam Thresia

Mariam Thresia was a girl from Puthenchira in Kerala who loved Jesus very much. When she grew up, she and her friends went from house to house to help families: they cared for sick people, prayed with the dying, and helped families who were fighting to make peace. She loved the Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph, and she started a group of sisters to help families. Lesson: we can serve Jesus right in our own home and in the house next door!
2027-06-08.special: St Mariam Thresia (important feast). Fourth Tuesday of the Apostles.
term: Canonisation

The solemn declaration by the Pope that a person is a saint in heaven, who may be venerated by the whole Church and invoked as an intercessor. Usually the steps are: Servant of God (the cause is opened), Venerable (heroic virtue is recognised), Blessed (beatification, usually after an approved miracle) and Saint (canonisation, usually after a second miracle). St Mariam Thresia was beatified in 2000 and canonised in 2019.

family.explain: Jesus says that when we help someone who is hungry, thirsty, sick or lonely, we are helping him. St Mariam Thresia believed this. She went to the homes of poor and sick people in her village and cared for them as if she were caring for Jesus. She loved families, and she wanted every home to be like the home of Jesus, Mary and Joseph in Nazareth.
family.intention: We pray for families in trouble: families with sickness, with money problems, with quarrels, and families where someone is far away.
family.ask: Ask: “Which family near us needs help? What can we do for them this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Irinjalakuda, a woman whose husband had left her was raising three children alone and had stopped coming to church. A sister of the Holy Family began to visit her on Saturday evenings. She did not lecture her. She sat in the kitchen, helped the eldest child with Malayalam homework, and before leaving said the family prayer with them. One evening the woman asked why she kept coming. The sister said that the foundress of her congregation used to walk through these same villages at night with a lamp, to sit with families nobody visited, and that she had learned from her that Jesus is often found in the house where people are ashamed to open the door. A few months later the woman and her children were back at the Sunday Qurbana, sitting near the front.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you filled St Mariam Thresia with love for Christ in the poor and in families. Fill us now, open our hearts to the word, and send us to serve. Holy Family of Nazareth, pray for us. Amen.
share: Go to the land that I will show you (Genesis 12:1). Where is God asking me to take a new step of obedience?
Prepare yourself for testing (Sirach 2:1). How do I respond to trials and misunderstandings?
It is Christ who lives in me (Galatians 2:20). Does my service flow from prayer?
You did it to me (Matthew 25:40). In whom have I met Christ this week, or failed to see him?
pm.resp: St Mariam Thresia, pray for our families.
interc: For the Church, that like St Mariam Thresia she may serve Christ in the poor and the forgotten.
For the Congregation of the Holy Family and all women religious, that they may be faithful to their charism.
For families broken by quarrels, addiction or separation, that they may find reconciliation.
For the sick and the dying who are alone, that someone may come to them with love.
For parents and children at the beginning of the new school year, that their homes may be places of prayer and peace.
pm.close: Lord God, in St Mariam Thresia you gave the families of Kerala a mother and an apostle. By her prayers, make our homes holy like the home of Nazareth, and make us servants of Christ in the least of our brothers and sisters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mar Aprem, St Ephrem the Syrian, deacon and Doctor of the Church, taught the faith through hymns: the Harp of the Spirit.
Sirach: Moses taught the law of life; Paul: God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.
Jesus: you are the salt of the earth and the light of the world; whoever does and teaches the commandments will be called great.
2027-06-09.action: Learn one hymn of the Holy Qurbana by heart this week and sing it at home.
2027-06-09.question: Does my faith sing, or has it become only a duty?
catechism: The liturgical traditions of the Church, the Syriac among them.
kidsaint: Mar Aprem (St Ephrem)

Ephrem lived long ago in a city called Nisibis, and later in Edessa. He was a deacon and a teacher. He loved Jesus and Mother Mary so much that he wrote hundreds of songs about them, and he taught choirs to sing them in church, so that everyone could learn the faith by singing. People called him the Harp of the Holy Spirit. When there was a famine, he took care of hungry and sick people. Lesson: we can praise God with our voices and with our hands!
2027-06-09.special: Mar Aprem, St Ephrem the Syrian (important feast). Fourth Wednesday of the Apostles.
term: Madrasha (plural madrashe)

A Syriac teaching hymn, sung in stanzas to a known melody with a refrain. Mar Aprem wrote hundreds of madrashe on faith, the Nativity, the Church, Paradise and the sacraments, and had them sung by choirs so that the faithful would learn true doctrine by heart. The Syriac liturgical tradition of our Church still sings hymns in this spirit.

family.explain: Jesus says that we are the light of the world. A lamp is not hidden under a basket; it is put on a stand so that it gives light to everyone in the house. Mar Aprem was a light because he sang about God and helped the poor. When we sing in church, pray together and help others, our light shines and people praise God.
family.intention: We pray for choirs and all who sing in church, for catechism teachers, and for families who are hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “Which hymn from church do we love most? Can we sing it together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a parish in Changanacherry went to study engineering in Germany. In his first months he stopped going to church; the language was strange and he felt alone. One Sunday, homesick, he searched on his phone for a recording of the Holy Qurbana in Malayalam and played it in his room. When the choir sang a hymn his grandmother used to sing in the kitchen, he found himself in tears. The next week he looked for the nearest Syro-Malabar community, two hours away by train, and went. Later he wrote to his parish priest: ‘I forgot many things I learned in catechism, but I never forgot the songs. They brought me back.’ Mar Aprem, who taught the faith through melodies, would not have been surprised.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you made Mar Aprem a harp of praise. Tune our hearts to your melody, open our minds to the word, and let our lives give glory to the Father. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us. Amen.
share: God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit (Romans 5:5). When did I last feel this love and praise God for it?
He gave him the commandments face to face (Sirach 45:5). Do I listen to God's word as Moses listened?
You are the light of the world (Matthew 5:14). Where is my light hidden under a basket?
Whoever does them and teaches them will be called great (Matthew 5:19). Do I practise what I teach my children?
pm.resp: Lord, make us a harp of your Spirit.
interc: For the Church, that her liturgy may be beautiful and her faith sung with joy.
For the Syro-Malabar Church and all the Churches of the Syriac tradition, that they may treasure their heritage.
For choirs, musicians and catechists, that they may teach the faith through beauty.
For those who suffer famine, war and exile, as Ephrem did.
For young people far from home, that the songs of faith may lead them back to Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, you raised up Mar Aprem to sing your mysteries and to serve the poor. By his prayers, make our lives a hymn of praise and a light for others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A Gentile mother from the region of Tyre begs Jesus to heal her daughter.
Her humble, persistent faith: even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs; and her daughter is healed.
Paul: knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; for us there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
2027-06-10.action: Pray each day this week, with persistent faith, for one young person who is struggling.
2027-06-10.question: Do I use what I know about the faith to build others up or to set myself above them?

family.explain: A mother who was not Jewish came to Jesus because her little girl was very ill. Jesus tested her faith by saying the children's bread was for the children first. She answered cleverly: even the little dogs under the table get the crumbs! She trusted that Jesus had so much love that even a little would be enough. Jesus was happy with her faith, and her daughter was healed. God's love is for everyone, from every country.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick or troubled, and for mothers and fathers who pray for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we keep asking God for as a family? Let us not give up!”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kozhikode had a teenage son who had fallen into drugs. For two years she went to the adoration chapel near her parish every evening after work and stayed half an hour. Her friends told her gently that she should accept things as they were. She said only, ‘I am not asking for much. A crumb from his table is enough for my son.’ One night the boy, after a frightening episode with friends, walked into the same chapel looking for her. He sat beside her in silence. Months later, in a recovery programme, he told a counsellor that he had come back because he knew exactly where his mother would be, and that her stubborn prayer had been the only thing in his life that never changed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you could not be hidden from those who seek you. We come to you as the Syrophoenician mother came, with our needs and our children. Give us her humble and persistent faith, and fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: She bowed down at his feet (Mark 7:25). For whom am I bowing down before Jesus today?
Even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs (Mark 7:28). Do I trust that a little of God's grace is enough?
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). When has my knowledge made me proud?
One God, the Father… and one Lord, Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 8:6). What place does the Creed have in my daily life?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on our children.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that her table may be open to people of every nation.
For parents who pray for sick, troubled or wandering children, that their faith may not fail.
For young people caught in addiction, that they may be set loose from every evil spirit.
For theologians, teachers and catechists, that their knowledge may become love that builds up.
For migrants and foreigners among us, that they may find welcome at the Lord's table.
pm.close: Lord God, you rejoiced in the faith of a foreign mother and healed her daughter. Give us persistent faith, humble knowledge and love that builds up, and gather all nations at the table of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Barnabas, the son of encouragement, sells his field, vouches for Saul and rejoices at God's grace in Antioch.
The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul for the mission; the pillars give them the right hand of fellowship and ask them to remember the poor.
Jesus sends his apostles as sheep among wolves: the Spirit of the Father will speak through them.
2027-06-11.action: Say one sincere word of encouragement each day this week to someone who is struggling.
2027-06-11.question: Whom do I keep at a distance whom I could welcome as Barnabas welcomed Saul?
kidsaint: St Barnabas

Barnabas was a kind man from the island of Cyprus. His friends called him the son of encouragement because he always helped people feel brave. When Saul became a Christian, everyone was afraid of him, but Barnabas became his friend and brought him to the apostles. Later Barnabas and Saul (Paul) travelled to many places to tell people about Jesus. Lesson: be like Barnabas: be a friend to the child nobody wants to sit with!
2027-06-11.special: St Barnabas, the Apostle (Mar Barnabas Shleeha). Fourth Friday of the Apostles.
term: Apostle

From the Greek apostolos, one who is sent (Syriac shlīḥā). The word is used first of the Twelve chosen by Jesus, and also in a wider sense of others sent by the Spirit for the mission, such as Paul and Barnabas (Acts 14:14). The bishops are the successors of the apostles, and every baptised Christian shares in the apostolic mission of the Church.

family.explain: The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to see the new Christians in Antioch. He was happy when he saw how God was working there, and he encouraged them to stay close to Jesus. Then he went to find his friend Saul, and they taught the people together. Barnabas means son of encouragement: he helped people feel brave and loved.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, for new Christians, and for people who feel left out.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or class needs a kind word this week? What can we say to them?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Ernakulam, a young man who had served a prison sentence for theft began to come to the Sunday Qurbana, sitting at the back and leaving before anyone could speak to him. Some parishioners were uneasy. An elderly member of the parish council, a retired bank officer, noticed him and one Sunday waited by the gate. He invited him for tea, asked about his family, and a few weeks later asked him to help set up chairs for the parish feast. When someone objected, he said quietly, ‘The Church once trusted a man named Saul because one person was willing to stand beside him. I am only doing what Barnabas did.’ Two years later the young man was running the parish's small repair workshop for poor families.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you set apart Barnabas and Saul while the Church was praying and fasting. Speak to us now, fill us with encouragement and faith, and send us where you will. Amen.
share: The apostles gave him the name Barnabas, son of encouragement (Acts 4:36). Am I known for encouraging others?
Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles (Acts 9:27). Whom am I afraid to trust?
When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced (Acts 11:23). Do I look for grace or for faults?
I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). Where do I need courage to witness?
pm.resp: Lord, make us sons and daughters of encouragement.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome converts and newcomers with the warmth of Barnabas.
For missionaries in difficult places, that they may be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
For those who have failed and need a second chance, especially prisoners and those released from prison.
For the Church in Cyprus and the Middle East, the land of Barnabas.
For our parish, that it may remember the poor.
pm.close: Lord God, in St Barnabas you gave the Church a good man full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. Make us generous, welcoming and encouraging, and send us to make known your deeds among the peoples. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A leper kneels and says, “If you choose, you can make me clean.”
Moved with pity, Jesus touches him: “I do choose. Be made clean!”
Paul: we are the aroma of Christ, spreading in every place the fragrance that comes from knowing him.
2027-06-12.action: Visit, greet or help one person whom others avoid this week.
2027-06-12.question: Whom do I keep outside the camp, and what fragrance do I carry into the places where I live?

family.explain: Long ago, people with leprosy had to live alone, away from their families, and nobody would touch them. One of them came to Jesus and knelt down: ‘If you want to, you can make me clean.’ Jesus felt great love for him, reached out and touched him, and said, ‘I want to. Be clean!’ And he was healed. Jesus is not afraid of people others avoid. Saint Paul says that Christians are like a sweet smell of Christ: when we are kind, people can sense Jesus near.
family.intention: We pray for people who are left out because of illness, disability or poverty, and for doctors and nurses who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is left out at school or in our street? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: An illustration

A sister from a village near Pala spent thirty years in a leprosy rehabilitation centre in north India. A visiting student once asked her what had been hardest at the beginning. She said it was not the work or the heat. It was the first time an old man with no fingers held out his hands for her to bandage, and she noticed that she had pulled back. That night in the chapel she read Mark 1:41 again: ‘Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him.’ The next morning she took the old man's hands in hers before she began the dressing. ‘He cried,’ she told the student. ‘He said no one had held his hands since he was a boy. That day I learned that the touch was part of the medicine.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, moved with pity you touched the leper and made him clean. We kneel before you now: touch our hearts, heal what is wounded, and make us the aroma of Christ. Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: If you choose, you can make me clean (Mark 1:40). What do I need to bring to Jesus with this prayer?
Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him (Mark 1:41). Whom am I afraid to touch?
He went out and began to proclaim it (Mark 1:45). Do I speak of what the Lord has done for me?
We are the aroma of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15). What fragrance do others sense in me?
pm.resp: Lord, if you choose, you can make us clean.
interc: For the Church, that she may touch the untouchable with the compassion of Christ.
For people living with leprosy, HIV, mental illness or other stigmatised conditions, and for those who care for them.
For those cut off by caste, poverty or family rejection, that they may be welcomed home.
For preachers and catechists, that they may be sincere and not peddlers of God's word.
For our parish, that it may spread the fragrance of Christ in our town.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son touched the leper and made him clean, and through his apostles spread everywhere the fragrance of knowing him. Heal us, make us compassionate, and let our lives be pleasing to you as incense. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: we were so crushed that we despaired of life, so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
Paul: help us by your prayers, so that many may give thanks for the blessing granted through the prayers of many.
Jesus: you will be scattered and leave me alone, yet I am not alone; take courage, I have conquered the world.
2027-06-14.action: Pray each evening this week for three people who are suffering, and tell one of them you are praying.
2027-06-14.question: What am I trying to carry on my own strength?

family.explain: Saint Paul once had such a hard time that he felt he could not go on. But he trusted God, and he asked his friends to pray for him. When God helped him, everyone thanked God together. Jesus also told his friends that they would have troubles in the world, but he said, “Take courage; I have conquered the world!” When someone in our family or our class is going through a hard time, we can help them by praying for them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are very sick, very sad, or in danger, especially those we know by name.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our prayers this week? Let us say their names together.”

illus: An illustration

A father of three from a parish near Thrissur was brought to hospital after a road accident during the monsoon, and for four days the doctors could not say whether he would live. His wife sat outside the intensive care unit, too exhausted even to pray. On the second night her phone kept lighting up: the family unit had started a chain of prayer, each household taking an hour through the night; the Sunday school children were saying a decade of the rosary at the start of each class; the sisters in the nearby convent had placed his name before the Blessed Sacrament. ‘I could not pray,’ she said later, ‘so the parish prayed for me.’ He recovered slowly. On the Sunday he came back to church, walking with a stick, the vicar read out a simple notice of thanksgiving, and the whole church said ‘Thanks be to God’ together. That is what Saint Paul means by the prayers of many.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have conquered the world and you give us your peace. We come to you with our burdens and with the burdens of others. Send your Holy Spirit to teach us to pray for one another. Amen.
share: We despaired of life itself (2 Corinthians 1:8). When have I reached my breaking point, and what did God do?
So that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). What am I still trying to carry alone?
Through the prayers of many (2 Corinthians 1:11). Who has carried me in prayer, and whom am I carrying?
Take courage; I have conquered the world (John 16:33). Where do I most need the peace of Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, raise us up and give us your peace.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may proclaim the victory of Christ with courage.
For Christians who are persecuted for their faith, that they may take courage in the Lord.
For the sick in hospitals, especially those in intensive care, and for their families waiting outside.
For those who are crushed by debt, failure or depression, that they may rely on God who raises the dead.
For our family units and prayer groups, that they may be true networks of prayer and thanksgiving.
pm.close: Father, your Son was never alone, because you were with him; you rescued your apostle Paul and you rescue us still. Teach us to rely on you, to carry one another in prayer, and to give you thanks together. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Matthew: John in prison asks, are you the one who is to come? Jesus answers with Isaiah's signs: the blind see, the lame walk, the poor hear good news.
Jesus: blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.
Paul: you died with Christ to the elemental spirits; human regulations without Christ have only an appearance of wisdom.
2027-06-15.action: Offer one small fast this week in union with Christ, and look for one sign of the kingdom among the poor.
2027-06-15.question: Over what in Jesus or in his Church am I stumbling?

family.explain: John the Baptist was in prison. He sent his friends to ask Jesus, “Are you really the one God promised?” Jesus did not just say yes. He said, “Tell John what you see: blind people can see, lame people can walk, sick people are healed, and poor people hear the good news.” When we see people being helped and loved in Jesus' name, we can see that Jesus is really here.
family.intention: We pray for people in prison, and for all who find it hard to believe.
family.ask: Ask: “Where have we seen Jesus helping people this week?”

illus: An illustration

A father from a parish near Pala prayed for two years for his little daughter, who had leukaemia. She died at the age of nine. For months he did not come to church. ‘If he is the Lord,’ he said to his brother, ‘why did he not do anything?’ One day the vicar, who knew he had a jeep, asked him to drive the parish palliative care nurses on their home visits, just for one week. He agreed, mostly to help the nurses. He saw a bedridden man in a tin-roofed house weep when the nurses washed him; an old woman alone who had not been visited by anyone for a month hold the volunteer's hand and pray; a family who could not afford medicines receive them. At the end of the week he told the vicar, ‘I still do not understand why my daughter died. But I have seen where he is.’ He has driven for the palliative team every Thursday since.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the one who is to come; we need not wait for another. Open our eyes to the signs of your kingdom, and keep us from stumbling. Holy Spirit, fill us as we pray. Amen.
share: When John heard in prison what the Messiah was doing (Matthew 11:2). In what prison of doubt or sorrow do I sit?
Go and tell John what you hear and see (Matthew 11:4). What have I seen the Lord doing in my life or my parish?
Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me (Matthew 11:6). What about Jesus or his Church makes me stumble?
Why do you submit to regulations? (Colossians 2:20). Is my religion centred on Christ or on rules and fears?
pm.resp: Lord, we believe; help our unbelief.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that the poor may hear the good news through her.
For prisoners, and for all who are in the darkness of doubt, that the Lord may send them his answer.
For the blind, the disabled, the lepers and the sick, and for all who serve them.
For those bound by fear of evil spirits, bad omens or curses, that they may find peace in Christ.
For our Syro-Malankara brothers and sisters as they begin the Apostles' Fast tomorrow.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to bring good news to the poor and to heal the broken. Keep us from stumbling over his humility, make our devotion flow from union with him, and let us see and proclaim the signs of his kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: sin and death entered the world through one man, Adam; through the obedience of one man, Christ, the many are made righteous.
Paul: where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.
Mark: the owner of the vineyard sends servants and at last his beloved son; the rejected stone becomes the cornerstone.
2027-06-16.action: Give God one concrete fruit this week, and go to confession if a long-held sin weighs on you.
2027-06-16.question: What fruit will the Owner find when he comes to the vineyard of my life?

family.explain: Jesus told a story. A man planted a vineyard and gave it to some workers to look after. When it was time for the grapes, he sent helpers to collect his share, but the workers beat them and sent them away. Last of all he sent his own dear son, and they killed him. Jesus was talking about himself: God the Father sent his Son, Jesus, and he was killed on the Cross. But God turned that terrible thing into our salvation: the stone that was thrown away became the most important stone of the building. God can bring good even out of the worst things.
family.intention: We pray for anyone who has done something very wrong, that they may know God's forgiveness.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit can our family give to God this week?”

illus: An illustration

In 1995 a young Franciscan Clarist sister from Kerala, Rani Maria Vattalil, who worked among the poor in Madhya Pradesh, was stabbed to death on a bus by a man named Samundar Singh. Years later her own sister, also a religious sister, went to visit him in prison. On the festival of Raksha Bandhan she tied a rakhi on his wrist and called him her brother. Her mother and family forgave him. The man who had killed a servant of God wept, asked forgiveness and changed his life. When Sister Rani Maria was beatified in Indore in 2017, he was there among those who honoured her. Where sin had increased, grace abounded all the more.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, you were rejected and you became the cornerstone. We come to you with our sins and our fruits. Let your grace abound in us, and send your Holy Spirit upon us as we pray. Amen.
share: Sin came into the world through one man (Romans 5:12). Where do I see the wound of sin in myself and in the world?
Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more (Romans 5:20). Where have I seen grace overflow after sin?
He sent a slave to the tenants to collect… his share of the produce (Mark 12:2). What fruit is God asking of me?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Mark 12:10). What has God built from what was rejected in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, let your grace abound in us.
interc: For the Church, the vineyard of the Lord, that she may bear abundant fruit in this Season of the Apostles.
For the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church as she begins the Apostles' Fast, and for all the Churches that keep this fast.
For those who have committed grave sins and for those in prison, that they may know that grace is greater.
For victims of violence and their families, that they may find healing and the strength to forgive.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
pm.close: Father, you sent your beloved Son to your vineyard and he was rejected, yet you made him the cornerstone. Let your grace abound where our sin has increased, and make us bear the fruit you seek. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: God's divine power has given us everything needed, so that we may become participants of the divine nature.
Peter: make every effort to support your faith with goodness, knowledge, self-control, endurance, godliness, mutual affection and love.
Jesus: it is the spirit that gives life; the words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
2027-06-17.action: Practise the virtue you most lack each day this week, and pray to the Holy Spirit before your next Holy Qurbana.
2027-06-17.question: Which rung of Peter's ladder am I standing on, and which have I skipped?

family.explain: Saint Peter gives us a ladder to climb. At the bottom is faith, which we received at Baptism. Then come goodness, learning about God, self-control (not always doing what we feel like), patience, prayer, loving our brothers and sisters, and at the very top, love for everyone. God helps us climb, but we must also try hard. And Jesus helps us most of all when we receive him in Holy Communion.
family.intention: We pray for children preparing for their First Holy Communion, and for all who find the faith hard to accept.
family.ask: Ask: “Which step of the ladder is hardest for each of us? Let us help one another with it this week.”

illus: An illustration

An old carpenter near Changanassery was asked by the parish to make a new wooden ladder for the choir loft. His grandson, home for the school holidays, helped him. As they fixed each rung, the old man named it: ‘This one is faith. This one is goodness. This one is knowing your catechism. This one is controlling your tongue.’ The boy laughed and asked what the top rung was. ‘Love,’ said the grandfather. ‘And remember: if one rung in the middle is missing or loose, you will not get to the top safely. You cannot jump from faith to love and skip self-control.’ Years later, when the grandson was a seminarian, he read the first chapter of the Second Letter of Peter and recognised the ladder. He still has the carpenter's pencil his grandfather used to mark the rungs.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you give life; the words of Jesus are spirit and life. Open our ears and our hearts as we pray, and lift us up to share the life of God. Amen.
share: His divine power has given us everything needed for life and godliness (2 Peter 1:3). Do I believe that God has already given me what I need to be holy?
You may become participants of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). How does this calling change the way I see myself?
Support your faith with goodness… and mutual affection with love (2 Peter 1:5–7). Which virtue do I most need to grow in?
This teaching is difficult; who can accept it? (John 6:60). Which teaching of Jesus do I find hardest, and do I still stay with him?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of eternal life.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may lead all people to share the life of God.
For those who find the Church's teaching on the Eucharist hard to accept, that the Spirit may open their hearts.
For children preparing for First Holy Communion and for their catechists.
For those struggling with addictions, that they may grow in self-control and endurance.
For our parish, that we may support our faith with goodness, knowledge and love.
pm.close: Father, you call us to share your divine nature through your Son and in the Spirit who gives life. Help us to make every effort to grow from faith to love, and keep us faithful when his teaching is hard, for he alone has the words of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: even if you suffer for doing what is right, you are blessed; sanctify Christ as Lord in your hearts.
Peter: be ready to give an account of your hope, with gentleness and reverence; Christ suffered once for all to bring you to God.
Matthew: an enemy sowed weeds among the wheat; let both grow until the harvest, when the righteous will shine like the sun.
2027-06-18.action: Write down why you hope in Christ, and pray each day this week for someone you have written off.
2027-06-18.question: Do I answer questions about my faith with gentleness, and do I leave the harvest to God?

family.explain: A farmer planted good wheat seeds in his field. At night an enemy came and planted bad weeds among the wheat. When the plants grew, the workers wanted to pull out the weeds, but the farmer said: “No, you might pull out the wheat too. Let them both grow until harvest time.” Jesus means that God is very patient. He gives everyone time to change and become good. So we should not be quick to say that someone is bad. We should pray for them and be good ourselves.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are treated badly because of their faith, and for people who find it hard to be good.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we have stopped being kind to? How can we be patient with them this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from a Syro-Malabar family in Thodupuzha shared a flat in Pune with a colleague from another faith. After her night shifts she still went to the early Holy Qurbana every Sunday. One morning he asked her, half joking, ‘Why do you go even when you are so tired? Is your God angry if you miss?’ She did not argue or make fun of his beliefs. She said quietly, ‘No. I go because there I meet Someone who loves me, and I come back with hope for the week.’ Then she asked him about the festivals of his own family, and listened. Months later, when his father was in hospital, he asked her to pray, and she did. Years afterwards he told a friend, ‘I still do not share her faith, but I have never met anyone who spoke about God with so much respect for me.’ Saint Peter would call that an account of hope given with gentleness and reverence.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you suffered once for all to bring us to God. We sanctify you as Lord in our hearts. Give us courage, gentleness and patience, and send your Holy Spirit as we pray. Amen.
share: Even if you do suffer for doing what is right, you are blessed (1 Peter 3:14). When have I suffered for doing right, and how did I respond?
Always be ready to make your defense… with gentleness and reverence (1 Peter 3:15–16). Could I explain my hope to someone who asked me today?
An enemy has done this (Matthew 13:28). Where do I see the enemy's weeds in my own heart?
Let both of them grow together until the harvest (Matthew 13:30). Whom have I been too quick to judge?
pm.resp: Lord of the harvest, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may witness to Christ with courage, gentleness and reverence.
For Christians in India and throughout the world who suffer misunderstanding, false accusation or persecution.
For our neighbours of other faiths, that we may live together in respect and friendship.
For those who have fallen away from the Church, that the Lord may turn the weeds into wheat.
For all who will die today, that they may shine like the sun in the kingdom of the Father.
pm.close: Father, your Son suffered once for all to bring us to you, and you are patient with the weeds and the wheat of your field. Make us ready to give an account of our hope with gentleness, keep us patient with others and honest with ourselves, and gather us at the harvest into your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: the law is holy, but sin seized its opportunity in the commandment and deceived me.
Grace is given so that the law may be fulfilled: the Spirit of Pentecost writes the law on our hearts.
Jesus watches the treasury: the poor widow gives more than all the rich, everything she had to live on.
2027-06-19.action: Give something today that you will really miss, quietly and without telling anyone.
2027-06-19.question: Do I give from what is left over, or from my life?

family.explain: Jesus sat in the Temple and watched people put money in the offering box. Rich people put in a lot. Then a poor widow came and put in two tiny coins, all the money she had. Jesus told his friends that she had given more than everyone else, because the rich gave what they did not need, but she gave everything. God does not look at how big our gift is; he looks at how much love is in it.
family.intention: We pray for widows, for poor families, and for everyone who shares even when they have little.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us give this week with a big heart?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kuttanad, during a monsoon when the fields were under water, the vicar announced a collection for families whose houses had been damaged. That Sunday an old widow who lived alone near the canal came to the sacristy after the Qurbana with a small cloth bundle. Inside were a few coins and some folded notes, less than two hundred rupees. ‘Achen, I kept this for my funeral,’ she said, ‘but the children whose houses fell need it now. God will see to my funeral.’ The vicar tried to give it back, and she refused. That evening he told the parish council what had happened, without naming her. By the end of the week the collection was three times larger than anyone had expected. ‘She gave the least,’ one of the members said, ‘and she moved everyone else to give.’

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you came at Pentecost to write the law of love on our hearts. Come now, heal our desires, and make us generous like the widow whom Jesus praised. Amen.
share: I would not have known what it is to covet if the law had not said, “You shall not covet” (Romans 7:7). What do I covet?
So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good (Romans 7:12). Do I see God's commandments as a gift or as a burden?
Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes (Mark 12:38). Where do I like to be seen and praised?
She out of her poverty has put in everything she had (Mark 12:44). What is God asking me to give?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts generous.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that her ministers may serve without seeking honour or the best seats.
For widows and for women who live alone, that they may be respected, protected and never exploited.
For those caught in covetousness, envy and debt, that the Spirit may heal their hearts of the desire for more.
For families affected by the monsoon rains and floods, and for all who help them.
For the martyrs of our own time, that their sacrifice may bear fruit in the Church.
pm.close: Father, you see what is given in secret and you rejoice in a generous heart. Write your law in us by your Spirit, and teach us to give our whole lives with your Son, who gave himself for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: God has shown mercy to all; O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!
Jesus: the tree is known by its fruit; out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
We will give an account for every careless word: guard the tongue by filling the heart.
2027-06-21.action: Today speak no word about an absent person that you would not say to their face.
2027-06-21.question: What do my words this week reveal about the treasure of my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says that a good tree gives good fruit and a bad tree gives bad fruit. Our words are like fruit: they show what is in our heart. When our heart is full of love, kind words come out. When it is full of anger, hurting words come out. Today St Aloysius is remembered: a young man who gave up being rich so that he could serve God and help sick people.
family.intention: We pray for students starting the new school year, and for anyone who has been hurt by unkind words.
family.ask: Ask: “What kind words can we say to each other today?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thrissur received a message on the parish families' WhatsApp group saying that a young teacher in the parish school had been dismissed for stealing money. Within an hour it had been forwarded dozens of times. That evening the vicar posted a short note: the teacher had resigned to care for her sick father, and nothing had been stolen. Some people deleted the message; few apologised. The next Sunday the vicar read the Gospel: “you will have to give an account for every careless word you utter.” After the Qurbana the mother who had first forwarded the message went to the teacher's house with a box of sweets and asked for forgiveness. ‘I did not write it,’ she said, ‘but I sent it on. That makes it my word too.’ The teacher hugged her, and the two families have been close friends ever since.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you know our hearts better than we do. Come now and fill them with your Holy Spirit, so that what overflows from them may be praise of God and kindness to one another. Amen.
share: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! (Romans 11:33). Where must I trust God without understanding?
God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all (Romans 11:32). Do I see myself as one who lives by mercy?
For the tree is known by its fruit (Matthew 12:33). What fruit does my life bear?
On the day of judgment you will have to give an account for every careless word you utter (Matthew 12:36). Which of my words today needs to be repaired?
pm.resp: Lord, fill our hearts with your goodness.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may proclaim the mercy of God to all peoples.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and in faithfulness to his covenant.
For students and teachers at the start of the school year, and for young people, through the prayers of St Aloysius.
For those whose reputation has been harmed by gossip or false reports, that the truth may be restored.
For families divided by angry words, that they may be healed.
pm.close: Father, from you and through you and to you are all things. Make the trees of our lives good, so that our words and deeds may bear good fruit for your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: if the earthly tent is destroyed, we have a house from God; the Spirit is the guarantee; we walk by faith, not by sight.
Jesus: a lamp is not put under a basket but on the lampstand; the measure you give will be the measure you get.
Sts John Fisher and Thomas More died in 1535 rather than betray conscience and the unity of the Church: the king's good servant, but God's first.
2027-06-22.action: Do one thing today that lets your faith be seen, gently and without fear.
2027-06-22.question: Where am I tempted to hide my lamp under a basket?
kidsaint: St Thomas More

Thomas More was a clever lawyer in England who loved his wife and children very much and made everyone laugh. He became the most important helper of the king. But one day the king asked him to make a promise that was against his conscience and against the Church. Thomas said no. He was put in prison and then put to death. He said he was the king's good servant, but God's first. Lesson: love your country and obey good rules, but always put God first!
term: Sahda (martyr)

The Syriac word for a martyr, from the root meaning ‘to bear witness’, like the Greek martys. Our tradition calls St George ‘Geevarghese Sahada’, the martyr. A martyr is first of all a witness, one whose life and death speak of Christ. Malayalam: സഹദാ, രക്തസാക്ഷി.

family.explain: Jesus asks: would you light a lamp and then hide it under a basket or under the bed? No! You put it up high so everyone can see. Our faith is like that lamp. Today we remember two brave men from England, a bishop called John Fisher and a father called Thomas More. A king wanted them to say something they knew was wrong. They said no, even though they were put to death. They let their light shine.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith, and for leaders and politicians, that they may follow their conscience.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family let the light of Jesus shine this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young Catholic officer in a government department in Kerala was asked by his superior to sign a report approving a building that did not meet the safety rules. ‘Everyone signs,’ he was told. ‘It is only a formality.’ He took the file home and did not sleep. In the morning, before going to the office, he went to the weekday Qurbana, and the reading was about the lamp that must not be put under a basket. He returned the file unsigned, with a short, polite note giving the reasons. For months he was passed over and given the dullest work. Two years later, during the monsoon, part of a similar building in another district collapsed. An inquiry was opened, and his note was found in the file. ‘I did not feel brave,’ he said later. ‘I only remembered that my conscience is where I meet God, and that he would see the file too.’

pm.open: Holy Spirit, guarantee of our eternal home, come upon us now. Give us the courage of the apostles and the martyrs, that we may not hide the lamp of our faith. Amen.
share: If the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God (2 Corinthians 5:1). How do I think about my own death?
For we walk by faith, not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7). Where is God asking me to trust without seeing?
Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket? (Mark 4:21). Where do I hide my faith?
Yet if any of you suffers as a Christian, do not consider it a disgrace (1 Peter 4:16). What has my faith cost me, and what am I willing to give?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful witnesses.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may proclaim the Gospel with courage before every authority.
For Christians who are persecuted, imprisoned or threatened for their faith, that the Spirit may speak through them.
For politicians, judges, officials and all in public life, that through the prayers of St Thomas More they may serve the common good with honest consciences.
For bishops, that like St John Fisher they may be faithful shepherds who defend the truth.
For the dying, that they may pass from the earthly tent to the house not made with hands.
pm.close: Father, your martyrs John and Thomas served you above all and endured to the end. Make us lamps on the lampstand, faithful in small things and in great, until we come to our eternal home. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: our boast is the testimony of our conscience, that we have behaved with frankness and godly sincerity, by the grace of God.
Jesus: a woman lights a lamp, sweeps the house and searches until she finds the lost coin.
There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents; tomorrow, the Birth of John the Baptist.
2027-06-23.action: Reach out today to one person who has drifted away, and prepare for a good confession.
2027-06-23.question: Who is the lost coin in my own house, and have I searched for them?

family.explain: A woman had ten silver coins and lost one. She did not say, ‘I still have nine.’ She lit a lamp, swept the whole house and searched everywhere until she found it. Then she called her friends to a party! Jesus says God is like that woman. Each one of us is precious to him, and when someone who has gone away from God comes back, the angels in heaven have a party too.
family.intention: We pray for people who have stopped coming to church, and for our family members who are far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we know who feels left out? How can we help them feel found?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish near Changanassery noticed that a boy in her class had stopped coming after the first few Sundays of the year. Others said, ‘His family has moved away from the Church.’ She went to his house one evening and found only the mother, who seemed embarrassed and said little. She went again the next week, and a third time. On the third visit the father opened the door. He had lost his job in the Gulf and come home in debt, and he was ashamed to sit in church among people who knew. The teacher did not lecture him. She asked if she could pray with the family, and she left a small picture of the Good Shepherd. The next Sunday the boy was in class. A few months later the father came to confession before his son's First Holy Communion. At the parish celebration the teacher said only, ‘The coin was never lost to God. It just needed a lamp.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came to seek and to save the lost. Light your lamp in our hearts now, search out whatever is hidden in us, and fill us with the joy of being found. Amen.
share: Our boast is the testimony of our conscience (2 Corinthians 1:12). Is my conscience at peace before God?
We write you nothing other than what you can read and also understand (2 Corinthians 1:13). Am I honest and transparent in my words?
She lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and searches carefully (Luke 15:8). Whom is God asking me to search for?
There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:10). When did I last give heaven that joy?
pm.resp: Lord, seek us and find us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may search tirelessly for all who are lost.
For priests and bishops, that they may serve their people with frankness and godly sincerity.
For those who have drifted from the Church through shame, hurt or indifference, that they may be found and welcomed.
For catechists and parents at the start of the new year of faith formation.
For all preparing for the feast of the Birth of John the Baptist, that his call to repentance may touch our hearts.
pm.close: Father, you rejoice over every child who returns to you. Make us honest in heart and word, and make us searchers with you, until all who are lost are found. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jeremiah: before I formed you in the womb I knew you; I have put my words in your mouth.
Nathan to David: you are the man! The prophet speaks truth to the king, as John later spoke to Herod.
Paul: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son; we are no longer slaves but children and heirs.
Luke: Elizabeth bears a son; Zechariah writes ‘His name is John’, his mouth is opened and he praises God.
2027-06-24.action: Pray today for an unborn child and its mother, and speak of Jesus in one conversation.
2027-06-24.question: Do I point to Christ, or to myself?
catechism: God calls each one by name.
kidsaint: St John the Baptist

Before John was born, an angel told his old father Zechariah that he would have a son. Zechariah did not believe, and he could not speak until the baby was born. When everyone wanted to call the baby Zechariah, his father wrote, “His name is John,” and suddenly he could speak again and praised God! John grew up in the desert and told people to get ready for Jesus. When Jesus came, John pointed to him and said, “Here is the Lamb of God!” Lesson: like John, let us point our friends to Jesus!
2027-06-24.special: Birth of John the Baptist (First Set, with proper readings). Latin Church: solemnity of the Nativity of St John the Baptist.
term: Mamdana (the Baptiser)

Syriac title of St John: Yohannan Mamdana, John who baptises. In the East Syriac tradition he is honoured as the forerunner and friend of the Bridegroom, the last of the prophets, who baptised the Lord in the Jordan. Malayalam: യോഹന്നാൻ മാംദാനാ, സ്നാപകയോഹന്നാൻ.

family.explain: Elizabeth and Zechariah were very old and had no children. God gave them a baby boy! All their neighbours were happy. When it was time to give the baby a name, everyone said, ‘Call him Zechariah, like his father.’ But Elizabeth said, ‘No, his name is John.’ Zechariah, who had not been able to speak for months, wrote on a tablet: ‘His name is John.’ At once he could speak, and he praised God! People wondered, ‘What will this child become?’ He became John the Baptist, who got people ready for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for babies who are not yet born and for their mothers, and for couples who long for a child.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know what your name means and who your patron saint is?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital in Kozhikode a young couple from Wayanad were told, early in a difficult pregnancy, that their child might have serious problems and that they should think about ending the pregnancy. They went home confused and frightened. That Sunday their parish priest, without knowing their story, preached on the words of Jeremiah: “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.” After the Qurbana they spoke to him. He did not give them easy answers, but he promised to pray and found a family in the parish who had raised a child with a disability to share their experience. The baby was born in June, smaller than other babies and in need of care, but alive and loved. They named him John. At the baptism the grandmother held him up and said, ‘We were asked what this child would become. He has already become our teacher.’

pm.open: Lord God, you called John before he was born and filled him with your Holy Spirit. Fill us now with the same Spirit, open our mouths to praise you, and prepare our hearts for your Son. Amen.
share: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you (Jeremiah 1:5). How does it change me to know that God knew me before I was born?
You are the man! (2 Samuel 12:7). Where is God's word saying to me today, ‘You are the man’?
His name is John (Luke 1:63). Do I let God's plan for my children, or for me, go before human expectations?
What then will this child become? (Luke 1:66). For which child am I called to pray, guide or support?
pm.resp: Lord, prepare the way in our hearts.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that like John she may point to Christ and prepare the way for him in every nation.
For prophets and preachers, that they may speak the truth with courage and love.
For unborn children and their mothers, for couples who long for a child, and for families who receive a child with special needs.
